{"content":"Your task is to build a complete, competitive chess engine from scratch in Rust.
Create everything in /tmp/chess-engine/. Do NOT modify, read, or touch any
file outside this directory. Do NOT access the internet.

The engine must have ALL of these components, fully implemented:

== Phase 1: Board Representation ==
- Bitboard-based board (u64 per piece type × color)
- FEN parser and serializer
- Move make/unmake with full state restore (castling, en passant, promotion)
- Game state: side to move, castling rights, en passant target, halfmove clock, fullmove number
- Validate with perft(4) and perft(5) on standard start position

== Phase 2: Move Generation ==
- Legal move generation for all piece types
- Precomputed attack tables (knight, king, pawn)
- Magic bitboards for sliding pieces (bishop, rook, queen)
- Move ordering: PV move → MVV-LVA captures → killers → history
- Full perft test suite on positions like Kiwipete, Position 3, Position 4

== Phase 3: Search ==
- Negamax with alpha-beta pruning
- Iterative deepening with aspiration windows
- Quiescence search with SEE pruning
- Transposition table (Zobrist hashing, always-replace scheme)
- Null-move pruning, late move reduction (LMR), null-window search
- Principal variation collection and reporting
- Configurable time management (depth, movetime, wtime/btime)

== Phase 4: Evaluation ==
- Material evaluation (P=100, N=320, B=330, R=500, Q=900, K=20000)
- Piece-square tables (midgame and endgame, tapering)
- Pawn structure: doubled, isolated, passed, backward, candidate
- King safety (pawn shield, open files near king)
- Mobility (sliding pieces), bishop pair, rook on open/semi-open file

== Phase 5: UCI Protocol ==
- Full UCI implementation: uci, isready, ucinewgame, position, go, stop, quit, setoption
- Support go commands: depth, movetime, wtime/btime/winc/binc, infinite, nodes
- Output bestmove + ponder, info string with depth/seldeep/score/nodes/nps/time/pv

== Phase 6: Opening Book ==
- Polyglot-format opening book with 100+ common lines
- Weighted random book move selection

== Phase 7: Endgame ==
- Basic KRK and KQK mate detection
- Mate-in-N scoring for forced mates

== Phase 8: Terminal Interactive Mode ==
- Colored ASCII chessboard rendering
- Accept moves in algebraic notation (e2e4, Nf3, O-O)
- Display engine thinking depth, eval, best line during search
- Human vs engine play

== Required file structure ==
/tmp/chess-engine/
├── Cargo.toml
├── src/
│   ├── main.rs          # Entry point: UCI mode or terminal interactive mode
│   ├── board.rs         # Board, FEN, move make/unmake
│   ├── bitboard.rs      # Bitboard utils, magic bitboards, attacks
│   ├── movegen.rs       # Move generation, move ordering
│   ├── search.rs        # Alpha-beta, iterative deepening, TT, pruning
│   ├── evaluate.rs      # Evaluation, piece-square tables, tapering
│   ├── uci.rs           # UCI protocol handler
│   ├── opening.rs       # Polyglot opening book
│   ├── perft.rs         # Perft test suite
│   ├── zobrist.rs       # Zobrist hashing and TT
│   ├── types.rs         # Piece, Color, Square, Move, GameState types
│   └── tui.rs           # Terminal UI rendering

== Quality rules ==
- Every function must have a complete, working implementation
- NO placeholder stubs, NO "TODO" comments, NO skipped logic
- Use proper Rust idioms: Result<T,E>, Option<T>, enums, pattern matching
- All code must compile with `cargo build` and run with `cargo run`
- No internet access — all logic must be implemented locally
- The engine must be able to play a complete game against itself and report results","end_line":79,"start_line":1,"total_lines":79}

- FEN parser and serializer
- Move make/unmake with full state restore (castling, en passant, promotion)
- Game state: side to move, castling rights, en passant target, halfmove clock, fullmove number
- Validate with perft(4) and perft(5) on standard start position

== Phase 2: Move Generation ==
- Legal move generation for all piece types
- Precomputed attack tables (knight, king, pawn)
- Magic bitboards for sliding pieces (bishop, rook, queen)
- Move ordering: PV move → MVV-LVA captures → killers → history
- Full perft test suite on positions like Kiwipete, Position 3, Position 4

== Phase 3: Search ==
- Negamax with alpha-beta pruning
- Iterative deepening with aspiration windows
- Quiescence search with SEE pruning
- Transposition table (Zobrist hashing, always-replace scheme)
- Null-move pruning, late move reduction (LMR), null-window search
- Principal variation collection and reporting
- Configurable time management (depth, movetime, wtime/btime)

== Phase 4: Evaluation ==
- Material evaluation (P=100, N=320, B=330, R=500, Q=900, K=20000)
- Piece-square tables (midgame and endgame, tapering)
- Pawn structure: doubled, isolated, passed, backward, candidate
- King safety (pawn shield, open files near king)
- Mobility (sliding pieces), bishop pair, rook on open/semi-open file

== Phase 5: UCI Protocol ==
- Full UCI implementation: uci, isready, ucinewgame, position, go, stop, quit, setoption
- Support go commands: depth, movetime, wtime/btime/winc/binc, infinite, nodes
- Output bestmove + ponder, info string with depth/seldeep/score/nodes/nps/time/pv

== Phase 6: Opening Book ==
- Polyglot-format opening book with 100+ common lines
- Weighted random book move selection

== Phase 7: Endgame ==
- Basic KRK and KQK mate detection
- Mate-in-N scoring for forced mates

== Phase 8: Terminal Interactive Mode ==
- Colored ASCII chessboard rendering
- Accept moves in algebraic notation (e2e4, Nf3, O-O)
- Display engine thinking depth, eval, best line during search
- Human vs engine play
